CVE-2026-126956.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding
CVE-2026-126956.description:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding.

Any constructed-form string element causes the decoder to recurse on the element's contents. The BER encoding controls nesting depth at four bytes per level, with no bound checked. Perl recursion is heap-allocated, so the process grows without a stack crash.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a small deeply nested constructed string.

CVE-2026-13575.title: HTTP::Session versions before 0.54 for Perl allow memcached command injection via unfiltered session ids in HTTP::Session::Store::CHI
CVE-2026-13575.description:
HTTP::Session versions before 0.54 for Perl allow memcached command injection via unfiltered session ids in HTTP::Session::Store::CHI.

The session id from the client's cookie reaches the CHI cache unchanged. The sibling HTTP::Session::Store::Memcached rejects ids that contain control characters, but the CHI store has no such check, and CHI does not escape keys for its memcached drivers.

With a memcached driver, a CR and LF in the session id end the cache command early, and the server reads the bytes after them as further commands.

CVE-2026-3583.title: Improper Token Revocation via OAuth2 Scope Enforcement in Multiple WSO2 Products [Disrupted Authentication Flows]
CVE-2026-3583.description:
When the `allowed_scopes` configuration is enabled, the OAuth2 token introspection mechanism does not immediately invalidate a token in the cache after a revocation request. This results in a scenario where an access token that was introspected immediately before a revocation request may be returned again to the client after revocation, until the relevant cache entry is cleared.

The security consequence is that a revoked access token may be re-issued to the client during the cache lifetime. While the re-issued token is not treated as valid for API authorization, affected users may be unable to obtain a new valid access token until the cache is cleared, which can disrupt authentication flows.

CVE-2026-77054.title: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in boneIO
CVE-2026-77054.description:
boneIO Black stores passwords, including the MQTT broker and web panel passwords, in cleartext. The GET /api/config endpoint returns the full configuration with sub-services passwords exposed. Any authenticated user can call the endpoint and access the administrative passwords in cleartext form. Critically, due to CVE-2026-77053 (authentication disabled by default), an unauthenticated attacker on the same local network can retrieve all passwords.

This issue was fixed in version 1.6.0: web panel passwords are stored as salted scrypt hashes in a file readable only by the service account, and the API and logs no longer return secret values. The MQTT broker password has to stay recoverable because the application presents it to the broker as a client; it is kept in a separate file readable only by the service account and is no longer exposed through the API.

CVE-2026-98985.title: namespace: check the mounts before reading their parents in pivot_root()
CVE-2026-98985.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

namespace: check the mounts before reading their parents in pivot_root()

path_pivot_root() reads the parents of new_root and of the caller's root
and checks whether they are shared before it checks that either mount is
in the caller's mount namespace. Only namespace_sem is held. That's fine
for a mount that is in the caller's mount namespace.

But new_root can be a file descriptor to a mount that has been unmounted
and that only the file descriptor keeps alive. If that mount stayed
attached to its parent when it was unmounted nothing pins the parent for
it. The final mntput() of the parent unhooks the children under
mount_lock alone and frees the parent afterwards:

pivot_root() close(fd), last ref on the parent
------------ ---------------------------------
ex_parent = new_mnt->mnt_parent
mntput_no_expire_slowpath()
__umount_mnt(new_mnt)
cleanup_mnt()
call_rcu()
IS_MNT_SHARED(ex_parent)

CVE-2026-99722.title: vringh: bound top-level re-entry into indirect tables
CVE-2026-99722.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vringh: bound top-level re-entry into indirect tables

In __vringh_iov(), the F_INDIRECT branch descends into the indirect
table and continues before the descriptor accounting runs. A top-level
indirect descriptor is therefore never charged to count. If such a
descriptor sets NEXT to point back at itself, returning from the
indirect table resumes at the same top-level descriptor, which is again
not counted, so the walk never makes forward progress.

Because count stays flat and indirect_count is reset to 0 on every
return to the top-level table, neither bound in the loop check trips.
A guest can spin the vringh worker at 100% CPU inside __vringh_iov(),
an uninterruptible host DoS.

top-level indirect descriptor is charged one top-level traversal step
before the walk descends into its table, bringing this re-entry under

CVE-2026-99757.title: btrfs: sysfs: restore NOFS context on early return in btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type()
CVE-2026-99757.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

btrfs: sysfs: restore NOFS context on early return in btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type()

btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type() sets up a NOFS context with
memalloc_nofs_save() because kobject_add() performs GFP_KERNEL
allocations deep in its call chain, and the function may be called
while holding a transaction handle or a lock required for a
transaction commit, where reclaim could deadlock.

Every other return path of this function calls memalloc_nofs_restore()
except the early return taken when another thread has already created
the kobject for the same raid index (this can happen when restriping).
Taking that path leaves PF_MEMALLOC_NOFS set on the calling task, so
all subsequent memory allocations performed by that task remain
restricted to the NOFS scope, which may lead to unexpected allocation
failures or deadlocks later on.

Restore the NOFS context before returning from that path.
